subject: SLA remediation request — proposed credit / make-good for latency impact (ClearData)
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit@cleardata.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Nina Park <nina.park@cleardata.ai>, procurement@cleardata.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency spikes / request for remediation credit

Diego —

Thanks for taking this urgent ticket. Over the last 48 hours we've seen sustained 2–3x p95 latency on our inference routes (text-gen-large) across us-west with a clear user impact (timeouts in our recommendation service). We filed support tickets but wanted to begin formal remediation discussions ASAP.

We need a proposal for credits or service make-good tied to this SLA breach. Our procurement team will need a formal memo showing the proposed credit, rationale, and acceptance steps. Attached is a brief timeline and a handful of sample errors from our side.

Requested by: ClearData legal/procurement — they prefer a one-time credit against Jan invoices or a 60‑day service credit.

Appreciate quick guidance — this is in-flight with customers relying on recommendations.

— Amit
CTO, ClearData AI

Attachments: prod-incident-timeline.pdf (summary), sample-logs.txt (attached separately)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@cleardata.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Jan 2028 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency spikes / request for remediation credit

Amit —

Thanks for the timeline and the flag. I'm sorry about the impact. We have an incident postmortem in progress; initial findings point to a serving config regression on a recent autoscaling policy change that produced resource contention on a small subset of clusters in us-west.

Short term: I can offer an immediate operational response (priority runbook, dedicated engineer during rollover window) to reduce risk while we remediate. For commercial remediation, I need exec sign-off for credits.

Proposed options for your procurement team (we're flexible):
- Option A: One-time invoice credit equal to 20% of January usage (simple, quick)
- Option B: 60 days of free service for the affected routes (applies as account credit)
- Option C: Customized credit using our incident severity bands — I can share a dollarized model.

I'm looping in Lauren and Marissa to get internal approval path started and to produce the formal memo you can share with procurement. I'll follow up with the incident doc once it's ready.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

----

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 26 Jan 2028 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency spikes / request for remediation credit

Diego / Marissa —

I reviewed the preliminary incident notes from infra (INF-2143) and the timeline Amit shared. The regression looks customer-impacting and crosses our P95 latency SLO for the affected routes for ~36 hours. We generally map that to the "major degradation" band in our SLA policy.

Budget guardrails: finance has asked we avoid open-ended credits. Proposed internal guidance to present:
1) If ClearData accepts an operational remediation + 30% invoice credit for January usage for affected routes, finance will approve up to $85k total credit without CEO sign-off.
2) Anything exceeding $85k or longer-duration credits (eg multiple months) needs Sean's approval.

Please prepare the dollarized model (expected usage during Jan for the affected routes + the 30% credit calculation) and a short memo for procurement. Diego — fill in expected dollars and attach the draft memo.

-Lauren
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 26 Jan 2028 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency spikes / request for remediation credit

Thanks — adding my recommendation from a customer success perspective. ClearData is a mid-enterprise account with expansion motion starting in Q2. I suggest we prioritize retention and predictability: offer 30% invoice credit for January (per Lauren) but also include one month of free Dedicated test capacity (equivalent SKU) as a goodwill gesture — that helps them rebound while maintaining short-term revenue.

If finance won't approve the Dedicated credit, alternative is to increase the invoice credit up to $95k (still below Sean threshold). I'll let you know if procurement pushes for cash refunds vs credits.

-Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jan 2028 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Request for exec approval — ClearData SLA concession (possible > $85k)

Sean —

Quick ask: ClearData experienced a 36-hour P95 latency breach in us-west between 2028-01-22 and 2028-01-24 caused by autoscaling config regression. Customer is asking for a remediation credit. Internal recommendation: 30% invoice credit for January usage for affected routes (est. $72k) + one month of Dedicated test capacity (value ~$24k). Total commercial impact = ~$96k.

Attachments: credit-model.xlsx (breakdown), draft-credit-memo.docx (procurement-ready memo), prod-incident-timeline.pdf (customer timeline).

If you approve, I will publish the memo to procurement and offer the credit. If you prefer we avoid the Dedicated month, alternate is a one-time invoice credit of $95k (cash impact). We need a decision to put in procurement by EOD Wed 31 Jan to avoid churn risk.

TL;DR: Approval requested for up to $100k in commercial concession to preserve renewal and expansion.

Thanks —
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 Feb 2028 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request for exec approval — ClearData SLA concession (possible > $85k)

Diego / team —

Thanks for the clear writeup and the model. I reviewed the attachments and the incident ticket. Given the customer impact and the near-term expansion opportunity, I approve the following:

1) One-time invoice credit of $75,000 to be applied to the Feb invoice (covers January impact).
2) One month of Dedicated test capacity for ClearData at no charge, capped at the SKU baseline we discussed (value recognized as $25,000, but not as a cash refund).

Please proceed with the procurement memo and get ClearData to sign acceptance of the credit and the operational remediation plan. Have legal sign off on the memo.

Also, please add a short clause in the memo that credits are non-refundable and applied to future invoices; record the concession code in HubSpot under deal DL-2028-0034.

— Sean
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
